text:
rachel.docs: Quick note from a docs pass: the 'hello-slim' quickstart auth snippet sets a Basic header: `Authorization: `Basic ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_TOKEN}``, but the SDK/hosted expects Bearer tokens. This will confuse new users.
dan.engineer: Ah, that's my bad copy-paste from an old internal example. Should be `Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_TOKEN}``.
yuki.devex: Also the snippet shows `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` in one spot and `REDWOOD_API_TOKEN` elsewhere. Might be worth a quick consistency sweep.
rachel.docs: Agreed. Can we fix both: header type + env var naming? Also add a 1-line PowerShell note since some users hit that during the workshop: `$env:REDWOOD_API_TOKEN = '...'`.
dan.engineer: Will do. Plan: 1) update snippet in quickstart, 2) add PowerShell block, 3) add a short migration note in the changelog and upgrade-guide.
pr-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1205 "fix(quickstart): auth header -> Bearer, env var consistency, powershell note" by dan.engineer
yuki.devex: Can you also add a tiny testable example showing how to inject a token in unit tests? A one-liner like `const client = new RedwoodClient({ token: 'test' })` helps readers.
dan.engineer: Good call. I'll add that in the TS example.
ci-bot: Docs build started.
pr-bot: PR ready for review (2 files changed).
rachel.docs: Quick review checklist: - update snippet playgrounds - run link-checker - update onboarding checklist item about env var rename if needed.
yuki.devex: I'll do the wording review once CI passes.
dan.engineer: Merged after CI green. Thanks everyone! :tada:
